newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Dec 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Dec 2.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Monday:
- Experts from 160 countries are gathering in Switzerland to rewrite international copyright agreements for the first time in the era of the personal computer and the Internet.
- Kmart did brisk business over the post-Thanksgiving weekend at its new Manhattan stores.

- When Sprint Spectrum wanted huge amounts of sophisticated electronic equipment to build a wireless telephone network, it went to Lucent Technologies and Northern Telecom, and then went to them for financing as well.

- In the race to develop a so-called network computer for Internet access, competitors battle over standards, missing the larger point that the focus of innovation in the industry will rapidly move beyond such relatively low-end products.
- With a new type of data base management software, Informix is trying to take market share from Oracle, its leading rival for such products.
- Columbia Pictures named Amy Pascal, the president of production at Turner Pictures, as its new president, replacing Lisa Henson.
- An investor received a patent for designing an adjustable vest with a microprocessor-controlled vacuum breast pump.
- Internet services are making strides giving computer access to the visually impaired.

- The recent agreement on a standard for the next generation of television sets is unleashing a consumer electronics revolution that will in time effect almost everyone in the country, and pit some of the world's largest corporations against each other in the competition to draw the blueprints for the future.
